hero: Exam: 75 airfoils from 34 designer families, 4×10⁴ ≤ Re ≤ 5×10⁵. AirfoilNet reads maximum lift (error 0.082) and the stall angle (1.8°) better than NeuralFoil (0.096, 2.2°) and the raw solver; NeuralFoil, trained on far more XFOIL runs, still wins on lift before stall, drag and moment.
examIntro: Run once, after everything else was frozen: all clean wind-tunnel runs of the 75 exam airfoils (vols 1-5 of the UIUC low-speed tests). Errors are averaged per run, then per airfoil, then over airfoils. Drag comes from wake-rake runs, which stop before stall, so there is no post-stall drag. The thin-airfoil line has no stall, so it has no maximum-lift or stall entry. The shaded cell is the best value in each row.
physIntro: The raw solver (mfoil, Ncrit 9) was run at one Reynolds number per exam airfoil, a fixed draw. Where it converges it is the most accurate thing here before stall (lift error 0.071). But it answered only 61% of the measured angles, and its last converged point sits well before the real stall, so its maximum lift is 0.22 off and its stall angle 4.0° early.
cov: AirfoilNet's raw 68% bars were too narrow on dev (they covered 33% of Cl, 36% of ln Cd, 17% of Cm), so each was widened by one factor fitted on dev only: ×2.77, ×2.44, ×4.75. On the exam the widened bars cover 69% of Cl points before stall, 74% of drag points and 83% of moment points (nominal 68%). The Cm factor was too generous on the exam.
twin: Before any network, the solver re-ran each dev airfoil at its tunnel Reynolds numbers (the twin). It gave no answer at 40-45% of the measured angles, mostly near and past stall: the Newton iteration of an XFOIL-class code fails when the boundary layer separates. At Re ≤ 10⁵ its polar stops 4.2° before the real stall and 0.11 below the real maximum lift, and its drag is 13% high; above 10⁵ its drag is 15% low. FX 63-137 gave no converged point at all. The drag trend became physics version p1c; the ratchet rejected it (+0.006 in simulation, short of the 0.01 margin), so the stall gap stays the main open rung.
ratchet: A rung is kept if it beats the incumbent on the frozen simulated set by more than 0.01 (skill = mean over Cl, ln Cd, Cm of 1 − MAE / MAE of a constant guess) and its error D on the real dev airfoils is at most 5% worse. Physics p1c brought a second frozen set (val2); every decision was re-taken on it and none changed. The first rung was never beaten: the operator network (DeepONet) lost to a plain MLP on this small bank, thin-airfoil anchors hurt after stall, and more simulations raised the simulated score but made the real dev airfoils worse.
recipe: Physics: mfoil (K. Fidkowski, MIT licence), an XFOIL-class code: linear-vorticity panels, two-equation integral boundary layer, e^N transition (Ncrit 9), lag-entrainment turbulence, wake, all coupled in one Newton solve. XFOIL itself could not be compiled here. We ported its hot loops to numba (same arithmetic; whole solves match the original to 1e-13) and fixed sharp trailing edges and Newton limit cycles.

Checks: the panel method matches the exact Joukowski airfoil to 0.1-0.2% in lift (Cp error 0.001); thin-airfoil theory for NACA 2404 to 0.02° in zero-lift angle; published XFOIL polars (NACA 0012, 2412, 4412) to 0.004 in Cl and 0.5% in Cd; NACA 2412 at Re 3×10⁶ lands near the classic NACA book values.

Simulations: 151 alpha sweeps (1,305 converged points) of 1,283 UIUC database shapes and blends, every tested airfoil and near-duplicate removed, Re log-uniform in 4×10⁴-6×10⁵. No noise injection: tunnel noise is not a public record here; the scatter is the solver's own.

Network: an MLP on polars. Inputs: thickness and camber at 24 stations (from an 18-parameter CST fit of the coordinates), log Re, and alpha. Outputs: Cl, ln Cd and Cm, each with a log-sigma, trained with β-NLL; 3 seeds, averaged (3 × 40,700 parameters). It never saw a wind-tunnel number.
Ratchet: 8 rungs on two frozen simulated sets and a 7-airfoil dev gate (4 families: Archer A18; Wortmann FX 63-137 and FX 74-CL5-140 MOD; Mueller M06-13-128, M6 65%, M6 85%; Trainer 60).
Twin test on dev located the physics gap: stall and laminar separation at low Re, where the solver stops answering.
Error bars widened once on dev (widen-only), then the exam ran once against NeuralFoil, the raw solver, thin-airfoil theory and the mean dev polar.
limits: Low Reynolds numbers only (4×10⁴-6×10⁵), incompressible, clean airfoils: no trips, flaps or roughness.
Small simulated bank (151 sweeps): drag before stall is 19% off on average (|ln ratio| 0.18), against 13% for NeuralFoil, which was trained on millions of XFOIL runs.
The solver does not converge near stall for many airfoils, so the network learned stall from incomplete polars. Its stall angle is 1.3° early on average.
Shapes outside the UIUC database family (very thick, very cambered, blunt) are extrapolation. The lab lets you make such shapes; the bars widen, but not always enough.
Moment error bars were widened ×4.75 on dev and cover 83% on the exam: too wide.
Data quality: the UIUC tunnel data carry their own corrections and uncertainties; volume 1 has no valid moment data.
